summary: Khenpo Dazer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and Shri Singha Shedra.

Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shechen Monastery under Khyentse Ozer, Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé, and Karsé Kongtrul, and served as Senior-Lehrer at Shechen Monastery.

Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (1933–2004) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima around 1951–1955, as well as under Yonten Gonpo, Khenchen Dazer, and several other traditional teachers.

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under Khenpo Gangshar and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later teaching at Rumtek Monastery and serving as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra.
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche (born 1946) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Bokar Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga. His students included Chatral Sangye Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Khenpo Shenga (1871–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Önpo Tenzin Norbu (~1890–1900) and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught at Shri Singha Shedra before becoming first khenpo at Dzongsar Monastery in 1918.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1960–1981), served as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery, and was spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery in 1992.
Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro (born 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (~1984–2004) and Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel.

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970), and taught at the University of Virginia (~1980).

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under teachers including Rasvir Das, later holding teaching posts at Lhasa Mentsikhang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was a Tibetology scholar. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held an academic post at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others in 2013.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at First Higher School, University of Tokyo, and University of Freiburg. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918; 1930–1945), dean at Hokkaido University, and professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed a PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (born 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held positions at the University of Leeds (~1980–2012) and at Lancaster University (~2012).

Kim Plofker (born 1964) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree, and held posts at Brown, MIT, Utrecht University, and Union College, where she became Associate Professor in 2019.
